subject: physics
title: Types of electromagnetic waves
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Types of electromagnetic waves — AQA GCSE Physics (8463) specification, section 4.6.2.1.
meta_desc: GCSE Physics (AQA) practice covering Types of electromagnetic waves, specification section 4.6.2.1.
final_note: You worked through Types of electromagnetic waves — 5 specification statements.

concepts.def: A transverse wave that transfers energy from the source of the wave to an absorber. Electromagnetic waves can travel through a vacuum, so they do not need a substance to travel through.
A wave in which the oscillations are perpendicular (at right angles) to the direction of energy transfer. All electromagnetic waves are transverse; sound waves, by contrast, are longitudinal.

The object or device that emits the electromagnetic wave and from which the energy is transferred away. Examples include the Sun, a lamp filament, a radio transmitter, the magnetron in a microwave oven and an X-ray tube.

The object that takes in the electromagnetic wave and receives the energy it carries. Examples include skin warmed by the Sun, water in food in a microwave oven, a solar cell, a receiving aerial and the retina of an eye.

Electromagnetic waves carry energy away from a source and deliver it to an absorber; no matter travels from the source to the absorber. Evidence of the transfer is a change in the absorber, such as a rise in temperature, a current in an aerial or a chemical change in the skin.

The electromagnetic spectrum runs without gaps from the longest wavelengths to the shortest. The seven named groups are convenient labels for regions of one unbroken spectrum, not seven separate kinds of wave, and the boundaries between them are not sharp.
A space containing no matter. Electromagnetic waves travel through a vacuum, which is why light, infrared and ultraviolet from the Sun reach the Earth across empty space.

All types of electromagnetic wave travel at the same velocity through a vacuum (space) or air. Radio waves, visible light and gamma rays from the same event therefore arrive at the same time; the groups differ in wavelength and frequency, not in speed.

The distance from a point on one wave to the equivalent point on the next wave. Wavelength is one of the two properties used to group the electromagnetic spectrum; radio waves have the longest wavelengths and gamma rays the shortest.

The number of waves passing a point each second. Frequency is the other property used to group the spectrum. Across the spectrum, going from long to short wavelength is the same as going from low to high frequency.
Going from long to short wavelength (or from low to high frequency) the groups are: radio, microwave, infrared, visible light (red to violet), ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays.

The group of the electromagnetic spectrum that lies between infrared and ultraviolet. Within visible light, going from long to short wavelength runs from red to violet, so red has the longest wavelength of the visible colours and violet the shortest.

concepts.term: Limited detection range of the eye
concepts.def: Our eyes only detect visible light, so they detect a limited range of electromagnetic waves. Radio waves, microwaves, infrared, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays all reach us unseen and need instruments, not eyes, to detect them.
The waves that form the electromagnetic spectrum are grouped in terms of their wavelength and their frequency — not in terms of their speed, their amplitude or how they are made.

mcqs.q: Which phrase best describes all electromagnetic waves?
options: Longitudinal waves that transfer energy to an absorber
Transverse waves that transfer energy to an absorber
Transverse waves that transfer matter to any absorber
Longitudinal waves that transfer matter to an absorber
mcqs.explain: The specification defines electromagnetic waves as transverse waves that transfer energy from the source of the waves to an absorber.

mcqs.q: A radio transmitter sends radio waves to the aerial of a car radio. Which statement describes the energy transfer?
options: Energy is transferred from the aerial to the transmitter.
No energy is transferred, only information is carried.
Energy is transferred from the transmitter to the aerial.
Energy is carried by particles that leave the aerial.
mcqs.explain: The transmitter is the source and the aerial is the absorber, so energy travels from transmitter to aerial.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the speed of electromagnetic waves is correct?
options: Gamma rays travel faster than radio waves in a vacuum.
All types travel at the same velocity through a vacuum.
Radio waves travel faster than gamma rays in a vacuum.
No type of electromagnetic wave can travel in a vacuum.
mcqs.explain: The specification states that all types of electromagnetic wave travel at the same velocity through a vacuum (space) or air.

mcqs.q: Ultraviolet and infrared leave the Sun at the same moment and travel through space to the Earth. Which statement is correct?
options: They arrive together because both travel at the same speed.
Ultraviolet arrives first because its frequency is higher.
Infrared arrives first because its wavelength is longer.
Neither arrives, because space has no air to carry them.
mcqs.explain: All types of electromagnetic wave travel at the same velocity through space, so equal distances take equal times.

mcqs.q: The electromagnetic spectrum is described as continuous. What does this tell you?
options: There are exactly seven separate wave types, with gaps.
The waves are all given out continuously and never stop.
There are no gaps between the groups of waves in it.
Every source gives out all seven groups at the same time.
mcqs.explain: A continuous spectrum runs unbroken from the longest wavelengths to the shortest; the seven names label regions of one range.

mcqs.q: Which list of groups is in order from longest wavelength to shortest wavelength?
options: microwave, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet
microwave, infrared, ultraviolet, visible light
infrared, microwave, visible light, ultraviolet
ultraviolet, visible light, infrared, microwave
mcqs.explain: This is the specification's own order for these four groups, running from long to short wavelength.

mcqs.q: A group of the electromagnetic spectrum has a lower frequency than infrared. Which group could it be?
options: ultraviolet
microwaves
X-rays
gamma rays
mcqs.explain: Microwaves lie before infrared in the low to high frequency order, so their frequency is lower.

mcqs.q: Compared with visible light, radio waves have:
options: a longer wavelength and a higher frequency
a shorter wavelength and a lower frequency
a shorter wavelength and a higher frequency
a longer wavelength and a lower frequency
mcqs.explain: Radio waves sit at the long wavelength end of the spectrum, which is also the low frequency end.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the colours of visible light is correct?
options: Violet light has a longer wavelength than red light.
Red light has a higher frequency than violet light.
Red light has a longer wavelength than violet light.
Every visible colour has exactly the same wavelength.
mcqs.explain: The specification lists visible light as red to violet within a run from long to short wavelength, so red is the longest.

mcqs.q: Which part of the electromagnetic spectrum can the human eye detect?
options: Visible light and infrared, which we feel as warmth.
Every group in the spectrum, from radio to gamma rays.
Visible light and ultraviolet, which tans the skin.
Visible light only, a limited range of the spectrum.
mcqs.explain: Our eyes only detect visible light and so detect a limited range of electromagnetic waves.

mcqs.q: A television remote control sends out infrared. Why can you not see the beam?
options: The infrared beam is too dim for your eyes to detect.
Your eyes detect only visible light, not infrared.
Infrared travels too quickly for your eyes to detect.
Infrared carries no energy, so there is nothing to see.
mcqs.explain: The eye's detection range is limited to visible light, so infrared passes unseen however strong it is.

mcqs.q: Food placed in a microwave oven becomes hotter. Which statement describes what happens?
options: Microwaves transfer heated matter into the food.
The food absorbs hot air produced inside the oven.
The food gives out microwaves that warm the oven.
Microwaves transfer energy from the oven to the food.
mcqs.explain: The oven is the source and the food is the absorber; the temperature rise is evidence of the energy transfer.

mcqs.q: Sunlight falls on a solar cell and the cell produces electricity. In this energy transfer, the absorber is:
options: the solar cell, which takes in the light
the Sun, which gives out the light
the sunlight travelling through space
the air between the Sun and the cell
mcqs.explain: The absorber is the object that receives the energy carried by the wave, shown here by the current it produces.

mcqs.q: Which statement about radio waves transferring energy is correct?
options: They carry information only, so no energy is transferred.
They transfer energy only once they slow down in air.
An aerial absorbs them, so energy reaches the aerial.
They transfer energy by pushing air particles along.
mcqs.explain: The alternating current produced in a receiving aerial is the evidence that energy has been transferred to it.

mcqs.q: The waves of the electromagnetic spectrum are grouped in terms of which two properties?
options: wavelength and frequency
wavelength and velocity
amplitude and frequency
velocity and amplitude
mcqs.explain: The specification states that the waves are grouped in terms of their wavelength and their frequency.

mcqs.q: A camper holds their hands near a fire and feels them get warmer. Which pair names the source and the absorber correctly?
options: source: the camper's hands; absorber: the flames
source: the hot air; absorber: the camper's hands
source: the fire; absorber: the surrounding air
source: the fire; absorber: the camper's hands
mcqs.explain: Infrared is emitted by the fire and taken in by the hands, whose temperature then rises.
